key_idea: The Möbius function of a short arithmetic progression a+gM is rewritten, through the Pellet/Stickelberger formula, quadratic reciprocity and resultants, as a quadratic character evaluated at the derivative of g. The character sums that result are bounded by computing the cohomology of a character sheaf on the space of polynomials, using vanishing cycles and perverse sheaves, which gives Betti numbers of size binomial(m-1,t).
reason: The proof combines two good ideas: Möbius values become character values, and short character sums are controlled through étale cohomology with explicit Betti numbers. Together these explain why cancellation occurs. The cost is a long chain of results (Chowla sums, level of distribution, Bombieri–Vinogradov-type estimates, singular series) and large explicit numerical constants on q, so the whole argument is a heavy multi-stage structure.
recognized: Sawin–Shusterman, 'On the Chowla and twin primes conjectures over F_q[T]' (Annals of Math)
